title: Simulation of Register Equality Test
statement: Let $A$ be a register-program instruction map with initial label $l_0$, let the oracle assign a Boolean answer to each decider and bit string, and let $x$ be an input bit string. Suppose labels $l,l_1,l_0'$, distinct registers $r,s$, and the instruction identity $A(l)=\operatorname{jeq}(r,s,l_1,l_0')$ are given. For any register valuation $v$ and output word, if the length of the binary expansion of $v(r)$ is at most the integer bound $W$, then the compiled program simulates this instruction from the configuration with label $l$ and valuation $v$ to the configuration with the same valuation and output and with label $l_1$ when $v(r)=v(s)$, and label $l_0'$ otherwise; at every intermediate configuration before the endpoint, no oracle call is pending and each work-head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: An instruction map A and initial label l₀
An oracle assigning Boolean answers by decider and bit string
A valuation v of all registers and an output word
Length of the binary expansion of v(r) is at most W
